2610.11450.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Coding Agent Playing ARC-AGI-3: Lessons for Continual Learning
2610.11450.paper_summary: We study how a coding agent learns across a sequence of abstract reasoning tasks. The agent runs on a frozen foundation model inside a fixed harness and acts by writing and running Python and shell scripts. It retains no state across turns other than its written artifacts, so every thought it forms, carries, corrects or abandons leaves a trace, where a thought is any belief, rule or plan committed to a file. We let the agent play ARC-AGI-3, a set of interactive reasoning games that provide no instructions. Each game is a sequence of levels, and a strategy that clears one level can fail on the next, so every new level is in effect a new task. The agent records what it learns as Python scripts and text notes, while the harness keeps a complete log of every action and observation. Our contribution is a measurement protocol that traces each thought through these files, from the task where it forms to the task where it is corrected or abandoned, applied to seven evaluation runs with three backbones from two model families. Scripts written for one task are almost never called again in a later task (33 of 630 references cross a task boundary), because most scripts embed the state of the current level. Instead, the agent rewrites its knowledge into new scripts, keeping the general rules and dropping the level-specific details, and abandons 74% of the scripts it wrote before a boundary. The notes, which only the model reads, are never revised: the agent appends without removing earlier claims, and the contradictions that accumulate are settled against the log. Because the log preserves everything, the agent forgets selectively, not catastrophically. The most costly error is a hard-coded value carried into a task where it no longer holds. These findings come from the files the agent wrote, without access to the model, and constitute a white-box analysis of how a coding agent continually learns.
2610.11450.paper_summary_zh: 我們研究一個編碼代理如何在一系列抽象推理任務中學習。該代理在固定的框架內運行一個凍結的基礎模型，通過編寫和運行 Python 和 shell 腳本來行動。它在每次回合之間不保留任何狀態，除了它寫下的文檔，因此它形成、攜帶、修正或放棄的每個想法都留下了痕跡，其中一個想法是任何寫入文件的信念、規則或計劃。我們讓代理玩 ARC-AGI-3，這是一組不提供指示的互動推理遊戲。每個遊戲都是一系列關卡，而清除一個關卡的策略在下一個關卡中可能會失敗，因此每個新關卡實際上都是一個新任務。代理將其學到的東西記錄為 Python 腳本和文本備註，而框架則保持每個行動和觀察的完整日誌。我們的貢獻是一個測量協議，追踪每個想法通過這些文件的過程，從形成的任務到被修正或放棄的任務，應用於七次評估運行，使用來自兩個模型家族的三個骨幹。為一個任務編寫的腳本幾乎不會在後續任務中再次被調用（630 個引用中只有 33 個跨越任務邊界），因為大多數腳本嵌入了當前關卡的狀態。相反，代理將其知識重寫為新的腳本，保留一般規則並刪除特定於關卡的細節，並放棄了 74% 在邊界之前編寫的腳本。只有模型閱讀的備註從不被修訂：代理在不移除早期聲明的情況下附加，累積的矛盾根據日誌進行解決。由於日誌保留了一切，代理選擇性地遺忘，而不是災難性地遺忘。最昂貴的錯誤是將硬編碼的值帶入一個不再成立的任務中。這些發現來自代理編寫的文件，沒有訪問模型，構成了對編碼代理如何持續學習的白盒分析。
